speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative check-up. Since you mentioned shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty, I need to ask: When did this pain start relative to your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic suppurative otitis media with recurrent mastoiditis and cholesteatoma.

The patient's history of recurrent ear infections, combined with post-tympanoplasty shooting pain triggered by chewing (suggestive of Eustachian tube dysfunction or referred pain from mastoid pathology) and pain when wearing earrings (indicating granulation tissue or bony growth in the external auditory canal), points toward a recurrence of cholesteatoma or persistent infection.

REQUEST IMAGES: High-resolution CT of the temporal bones.
